Pi: latent connected partition H individuates low-level graph states into source-defined high-level clusters
C: connected-cluster constraint and graph-consistency/admissibility conditions on H; generic experimental task conditions remain L_ctx
Q: shortest-path/planning objective and hierarchy-conditioned behavioral criteria
P_in: graph topology, start-goal/task distribution and reward evidence
P_out: planned path/navigation choice and hierarchy-conditioned readout
K: low-to-high source abstraction induced by H
explicit HBFS planning over high-level and relevant low-level graph structure
T: MCMC iteration and source-defined planning/search order
rho/O: path/choice behavior, inferred hierarchy/readout and experiment-specific observations

L_ctx: Source task/experimental conditions remain explicit and are not retyped into C solely because they are called conditions.
L_claim: Negative, null, approximation, genealogy and epistemic qualifications remain claim-layer assertions rather than added system roles.
L_formal: Algorithmic inference/search/fitting carriers are kept distinct from source-supported cognitive state; formal plumbing cannot create a coordinator.

system_world_experiment.system: inferred internal hierarchy H, posterior representation and planning process
system_world_experiment.world: environment graph G, low-level states/edges, start/goal/task/reward distribution
system_world_experiment.boundary: world graph is observed/model input; H is source-defined internal representation; MCMC/HBFS bookkeeping is not promoted beyond source role

source_defined_coordination_or_gating: hierarchy H supplies source-defined abstraction shared by inference and planning
HBFS uses bridge/high-level structure for source-defined route planning
